knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Flushing and reporting are the required first steps. The other options delay care or add a non-standard product.
Washing, free bleeding without squeezing, and immediate reporting match the source. The other options squeeze the wound, add antiseptic as a first step, or delay the report.
Those details are what follow-up needs. Contact details alone or blame are not what the record requires.

practicalCriteria: Given a mock splash to the eye, the learner names the flushing method and the person to report to.
The learner completes a mock exposure record with every required detail.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation of the mock response
stopWorkCriteria: An exposure has occurred and the worker has not yet been able to wash or flush
The worker is asked to continue a task while the exposure report is still open
